extracted.intended_audience: Harvard faculty, staff, students, and administrators planning or coordinating educational programs or corporate engagements
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional guidance on when and how to apply Restricted Party and Export Controls Screening to Harvard educational programs, and the policy criteria and review processes governing corporate engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted Party and Export Controls Screening for educational programs
rubrics_metrics.description: To support compliance with U.S. export controls and sanctions, Harvard has in place Restricted Party and Export Controls Screening for educational programs that may involve international participation or restricted content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines apply to a range of academic offerings including, but not limited to executive and professional education, online courses, conferences, and workshops, and are intended to help safeguard the University’s educational activities from regulatory risks. For more information, refer to the Screening Requirements Bulletin which outlines when screening is necessary; supporting materials include FAQs and a quick-reference infographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: When screening is necessary (reference: Screening Requirements Bulletin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Screening requirements are described in the Screening Requirements Bulletin, which outlines when screening is necessary for educational programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Screening Requirements Bulletin and supporting materials (FAQ, quick-reference infographic) to determine applicability and procedures. Contact your School’s Export Control Administrator (ECA) with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to consult resources and contact Export Control Administrator (ECA)
rubrics_metrics.description: All faculty, staff, and students planning or coordinating educational activities are encouraged to consult these resources and contact their School’s Export Control Administrator (ECA) with any questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before proceeding with programs that may involve international participation or restricted content, program planners should review the bulletin and supporting materials and obtain screening guidance from the ECA to mitigate regulatory risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate engagement review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Harvard has established robust policies around corporate engagement and processes for reviewing potential engagements to ensure that they support academic freedom and core institutional values, avoid conflicts of interest, and align with the needs and priorities of the University and its constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Provost’s Office convened ad hoc committees (Corporate Relations Research Policy Committee and Corporate Relations Researcher Engagement Committee) to review policies, processes, and support; their joint report (June 2024) contains key recommendations for corporate engagement practice and review. Use these policies/processes to evaluate potential engagements against academic freedom, institutional values, conflict-of-interest avoidance, and alignment with university priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor federal agency policy updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Many federal agencies are updating their policies and solicitations in response to recent Executive Orders and related federal agency directives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the OVPR page for the latest updates on agency-specific orders and requirements and incorporate those updates into program planning and compliance reviews.
